decision: adopted the other thread's open-data map pipeline as the base instead of starting over
why: it already turns Natural Earth and World Bank data into a 16k-cell land grid plus 4.4k sea zones for 193 nations

decision: wrote the shared core before fanning out: one JSON World, map graph, engine loop, testkit
why: ten parallel workers need one contract to code against or the merge falls apart

decision: cross-system signals go on world.theater with one named writer per field; private state on per-system slices via module augmentation
why: lets workers run in parallel without editing the same files

decision: launched 13 parallel workers each in its own worktree: catalog, nations, land, air, naval, logistics, economy, strategic, diplomacy+AI, UI, and 3 order-of-battle regions
why: seams are folders; each worker owns one so merges stay clean

decision: started order-of-battle workers before the catalog exists, using a shared snake_case id convention
why: waiting would serialize the longest data task; id mismatches get reconciled by a validation test at merge

decision: merged nation profiles (193 nations, 30 treaties, FAS warheads)
why: worker stayed in its folder; 15 tests, mutation-checked by breaking data four times

decision: kept warheads = FAS military stockpile, not total inventory
why: retired warheads cannot be launched; inventory kept in nuclearForces

decision: pair opinion = mean of both directions
why: createWorld overwrote one direction with the other, per the nations worker

decision: merged land movement and combat (Lanchester mix, Dupuy terrain, encirclement)
why: 3:1 vs entrenched breaks in ~3.5 days at ~2%/day attacker loss, matching Ukraine-era rates

decision: merged logistics (bloc-shared supply networks, railhead distance decay, repair, replacement)
why: truck radius calibrated to van Creveld ~300 km; pockets get zero

decision: moved timing assertions to *.perf.test.ts run serially by npm run perf
why: logistics budget test passed alone but failed in the parallel suite with 10 agents on 4 cores

decision: merged strategic: nuclear release, effects, fallout, missile defense, space, cyber, nuclear winter
why: 300 kt airburst on NYC ~880k dead, NUKEMAP order of magnitude

decision: merged map UI: engine in web worker, diffed snapshots, canvas Equal Earth map, command panels
why: verified in Chromium via Playwright, no console errors

decision: merged economy + defense industry (ramp lags, input dependencies, blockade, sanctions, manpower)
why: Japan under 80% blockade loses 40% GDP after stocks run out, US barely affected; 9 mutation checks caught

decision: merged naval: Hughes salvo, sub/ASW, mines, chokepoint trade blockade, amphibious landings
why: reproduces Moskva sinking; Red Sea ~2 interceptors per drone; opposed Taiwan landing >30% loss

decision: merged air/missile: sorties, stealth BVR, IADS salvo intercepts, strikes, SEAD
why: calibration table: Shahed 79%, PAC-3 vs Kinzhal 73%, Iran Apr 2024 98.6%

decision: merged diplomacy (treaty cascades, escalation, war support, capitulation) and AI (strategy, fronts, 3:1 attacks, doctrine-gated nuclear use)
why: 18 tests incl. NFU never first-uses; mutation-checked

decision: merged Russia/China/PRK/Iran/CSTO order of battle (695 formations)
why: 24 per-nation totals within 15% of IISS/CMPR; placement test caught 35 bad coordinates

decision: wired all systems; treaty reliability = 1-(1-commitment)(1-member reliability)
why: a product made USA and DEU decline Art. 5 for Poland while Malta joined

decision: merged Asia/Middle East/Americas/Africa ORBAT (32 nations hand-modelled) plus generator for 124 more
why: every nation in the world now has forces; per-nation totals within 15% of IISS

decision: built reconcile-ids script; 613 ORBAT ids missing from catalog; fanned out 4 workers by system family to alias or add each
why: units with unknown kit are dropped at placement, so the war would be fought by a fraction of real forces

decision: profiled real scenarios: 96 ms/tick peace, 143 ms war, logistics 55-70 ms mean and 360 ms worst
why: per-system timing on the full 2,151-formation world

decision: merged US/NATO/Ukraine ORBAT (856 formations, 32 nations)
why: totals within 10% of IISS; 3 deliberate data breaks caught

decision: added 332 island cells (>200 km2) to the map grid; replaced hardcoded node ids in tests with coordinates
why: Guam, Okinawa, Hawaii bases were landing in the sea; the west ORBAT test's stale-allowlist check confirmed the fix
result: Guam/Okinawa/Oahu now land; Diego Garcia still open water

decision: added a conventions test that fails if any unit test file reads the clock
why: second timing test (ai-perf) flaked in the parallel suite; a rule in the brief was not enough

decision: merged land armor reconciliation: 67 new vehicles, 36 aliases, generic truck
why: units fielding T-72M1, M113, Leopard 1 etc. were being dropped

decision: merged air reconciliation: 54 aircraft, 97 aliases; shahed_136 kept as one drone per rail, not aliased to a 5-rail launcher
why: aliasing would have multiplied drones 5x and invented trucks

decision: merged land fires reconciliation: 75 platforms, 50 munitions, 101 aliases; df21_tel made conventional
why: aliasing to the nuclear DF-21A put 12 warheads in Saudi hands

decision: first full Ukraine run (14 days) exposes: France, Lithuania, China, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan join the war; front moves ~48,000 km2 in 2 weeks vs ~4,000 km2/year real; RUS personnel casualties 643 vs ~15,000 expected; 7,848 RUS missiles fired
why: measured on the real world with every order of battle

decision: merged final reconciliation: 0 missing ids, 3,152 formations placed; added a gate test that fails on any unresolved ORBAT id or dangling alias
why: keeps catalog and orders of battle in lockstep from now on

decision: launched 5 calibration workers (politics, ground, air/missile, naval+Taiwan, economy), each owning its system folder and encoding cited bands as *.realism.test.ts
why: outcomes must match Oryx/ISW/CSIS/RAND references on real scenario runs, not fixtures
